text:
paige (marketing): Quick kickoff: EchoLab Workshop — community tutorial + hands-on lab + micro-benchmark. Plan: short blog post, gated live lab, 90s social clip. Target launch 2 weeks from now. Need benchmark framing (what story to tell), webinar hook, RSVP gating question, and follow-up routing.

 diego (devrel): Love the idea. For the bench narrative, let's frame around a concrete dev pain: multi-doc retrieval + reranking latency under a 3-turn assistant flow. Show tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, and a tiny cost estimate per 1k tokens. Make the visual a single combined bar + line chart.

 tara (growth): RSVP gating idea: ask one short question: "Primary challenge" -> (prototyping, latency, cost, infra). Map answers to nurture tracks: proto, perf, cost, infra. We'll attach utm_source to each campaign link.

 yuki (engineer): Repo ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/echolab-workshop. Lab includes Dockerfile, k8s manifest, and bench tool: `bin/bench_run --scenario rerank --concurrency 8 --seq 128`. It outputs `summary.json` and a small CSV.

 nora (events): Webinar plan: 30m total — 12m live lab walk-through, 10m bench story & tuning tips, 8m Q&A. Wed 10am PT preferred. Speakers: paige for product framing, diego demo, yuki infra notes. We'll produce a 90s highlight clip.

 build-bot: Staging preview deployed at https://echolab-preview.redwood.ai — pipeline #712 passed :white_check_mark:

 diego (devrel): Draft copy: Blog blurb: "EchoLab Workshop: run a hands-on lab, reproduce a micro-benchmark for reranking latency, and learn pragmatic tuning steps for lower cost and better tail latency." Social: "EchoLab Workshop — 20m lab + reproducible micro-benchmark. Live Wed 10am PT. RSVP: https://redwood.ai/echolab (utm=tw)"

 paige (marketing): small tweak: emphasize "reproducible micro-benchmark" and call out "includes reranking script and Docker + k8s manifests" in blog. For social, keep short and punchy.

 tara (growth): Routing: send RSVPs to `/workflows/echolab-lab`. Tag contacts `echolab_rsvp`. Post-webinar plan: immediate email with repo + `summary.json` link, then segmented follow-up per challenge track at 48h with tailored next steps.

 yuki (engineer): We'll run the bench live in the demo: `bin/bench_run --scenario rerank --save /tmp/echolab_report.json && aws s3 cp /tmp/echolab_report.json s3://redwood-echolab/reports/`. Sample output JSON: `{"tokens_per_sec": 420, "median_latency_ms": 45, "p95_latency_ms": 110, "cost_per_1k_tokens": "$0.08"}`. We'll note instance type used (dev: g5, scale: a100).

 nora (events): Ops checklist: 1) landing page + RSVP form 2) slides & rehearsal 3) 90s highlight clip 4) UTMs + tracking 5) infra on-call. Who's owning slides?

 paige (marketing): I'll own slides + main blog. diego owns demo script & social snippets. tara owns registration flow + nurtures. yuki infra + report format. nora events ops.

 diego (devrel): I'll add 3 short prompts to the lab (cold vs warmed cache, rerank-heavy, long-context) so we can show real differences in tail latency and tokens/sec. Also will record a 90s cut during rehearsal.

 tara (growth): Suggested A/B subject lines for the post-webinar email: A) "Your EchoLab micro-benchmark & lab" B) "How we hit 45ms median latency — EchoLab results". I'll split 50/50 and measure opens/clicks.

 yuki (engineer): Note: bench numbers fluctuate by model and infra. We'll include a small table comparing dev (g5) vs prod (a100) expected ranges and annotate the `summary.json` with `instance_type` and `model_id` for reproducibility.

 diego (devrel): Quick ask: can we create a tiny interactive snippet on the landing page showing the p50/p95 numbers so visitors see the benchmark highlight before registering? If yes, who's on frontend?

 paige (marketing): Good idea. we'll mock a static preview first (image + values). frontend help later. For now, add to the PR checklist.

 build-bot: Calendar invite created: 2026-09-ECHOLAB-01. Reminder scheduled for speakers.

 nora (events): Rehearsal one day before, 30m. Please confirm availability.

 paige (marketing): Confirmed. Final note: include a demo CTA at the end "Run this lab now" so post-webinar email conversion is high. Dropping GH issue links and landing draft here when ready. :rocket:
